name: Magnetite

matrix.title: Octahedron ↔ dodecahedron
matrix.subtitle: Rows run from the octahedron {111} to the rhombic dodecahedron {110}. Columns add cube {100} or trapezohedron {311} truncations.
matrix.note: Form letters follow Dana (1892). m = {311} is taken from the spinel-group convention. No field study systematically ties octahedral versus dodecahedral magnetite to temperature or fO₂. The best direct evidence is experimental: Hirano & Somiya (1976) found {110} gaining over {111} under more reducing conditions. Spinel-law twins on {111} and biogenic habits are not modelled.

about:
Magnetite matters to two communities. It is a (U–Th)/He thermochronometer for mafic volcanic rocks and serpentinites, and it is the main remanence carrier in paleomagnetism. Its habit is most commonly the octahedron o{111}. The rhombic dodecahedron d{110} is the next most common and is often striated by o/d oscillation; the cube a{100} is rare (Dana 1892). A BFDH ranking from the Fd3̄m reflection conditions predicts the same order, {111} > {110} > {311} > {100}.

Grain shape matters for both uses. In (U–Th)/He dating, grain size and fragment geometry control α-ejection and which population a date belongs to. In rock magnetism, elongation widens the single-domain size range, and truncated octahedra are the standard shapes in micromagnetic models.

habits.name: Octahedral
habits.text: o{111} alone or with small d truncations, the normal habit (rows M1–M2).

habits.name: Dodecahedral
habits.text: d{110} dominant, often striated parallel to the d/o edge (rows M4–M5).

habits.name: Combinations
habits.text: Octahedron plus dodecahedron, rarely cubo-octahedra (column b) or with m{311} (column c).

habits.name: Not modelled
habits.text: Spinel-law twins flattened on {111}, and biogenic or meteoritic habits (elongated prismatic, truncated hexa-octahedral).

references.citation: Fleet, M.E. (1981). The structure of magnetite. Acta Crystallographica B 37, 917–920.
Hirano, S., Somiya, S. (1976). Hydrothermal crystal growth of magnetite in the presence of hydrogen. Journal of Crystal Growth 35, 273–278.
references.note: Experiments in which {110} gains over {111} at higher H<sub>2</sub>, i.e. more reducing conditions. The clearest habit–condition link.

references.citation: Blackburn, T.J., Stockli, D.F., Walker, J.D. (2007). Magnetite (U–Th)/He dating and its application to the geochronology of intermediate to mafic volcanic rocks. Earth and Planetary Science Letters 259, 360–371.
references.note: The founding magnetite (U–Th)/He method. α-ejection is handled by air-abrading grain rims, so grain geometry enters directly.

references.citation: Cooperdock, E.H.G., Stockli, D.F. (2016). Unraveling alteration histories in serpentinites and associated ultramafic rocks with magnetite (U-Th)/He geochronology. Geology 44, 967–970.
references.note: Interior fragments of large grains record cooling, while small grains record later hydrothermal growth. Grain size and geometry guide interpretation.

references.citation: Schwartz, S., Gautheron, C., Ketcham, R.A., et al. (2020). Unraveling the exhumation history of high-pressure ophiolites using magnetite (U-Th-Sm)/He thermochronometry. Earth and Planetary Science Letters 543, 116359.
references.note: Euhedral and pseudo-euhedral grain shapes give distinct date populations.

references.citation: Fanale, F.P., Kulp, J.L. (1962). The helium method and the age of the Cornwall, Pennsylvania magnetite ore. Economic Geology 57, 735–746.
references.note: The earliest helium dating of magnetite.

references.citation: Butler, R.F., Banerjee, S.K. (1975). Theoretical single-domain grain size range in magnetite and titanomagnetite. Journal of Geophysical Research 80, 4049–4058.
references.note: Elongation widens the single-domain size range, so grain shape controls remanence stability.

references.citation: Muxworthy, A.R., Williams, W. (2006). Critical single-domain/multidomain grain sizes in noninteracting and interacting elongated magnetite particles. Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth 111.
references.note: Micromagnetic SD/MD thresholds as a function of particle elongation.

references.citation: Nagy, L., Williams, W., Muxworthy, A.R., Fabian, K., Almeida, T.P., Ó Conbhuí, P., Shcherbakov, V.P. (2017). Stability of equidimensional pseudo-single-domain magnetite over billion-year timescales. PNAS 114, 10356–10360.
references.note: Vortex-state equant grains are stable remanence carriers.

references.citation: Devouard, B., Pósfai, M., Hua, X., Bazylinski, D.A., Frankel, R.B., Buseck, P.R. (1998). Magnetite from magnetotactic bacteria: size distributions and twinning. American Mineralogist 83, 1387–1398.
references.note: Quantitative size, shape and twin statistics of biologically controlled magnetite.

references.citation: Thomas-Keprta, K.L., Clemett, S.J., Bazylinski, D.A., et al. (2001). Truncated hexa-octahedral magnetite crystals in ALH84001: Presumptive biosignatures. PNAS 98, 2164–2169.
references.note: Crystal habit used as a diagnostic of how the magnetite formed.

references.citation: Dunlop, D.J., Özdemir, Ö. (1997). Rock Magnetism: Fundamentals and Frontiers. Cambridge University Press.
references.note: Reference text on grain size, shape and domain state.
